text:
sasha: ok folks — planning a replay-harness + synthetic load pass tomorrow. need alignment on kernel selection, batching heuristics, KV-cache warmup, and exact metric defs we’ll publish (TTFT / TPOT / p95/p99 / goodput vs QPS).
marcus: quick Q — target model/config for the run?
sasha: 8k context 16b activations, try fp16 + int8-quant profiles. run 1: 8k seq, run 2: 2k seq (tail behavior).
anya: kernel selection note: we should collect per-layer kernel timings (conv/attention/ffn). dump kernel names + chooser decision for each step so we can reproduce why a kernel was picked.
dex: batching heuristics — we need deterministic batch scheduling for apples-to-apples. replay harness should replay original interarrival times and preserve batching boundaries. synthetic can stress extremes but not replace replay.
olga: KV-cache warmup: include a warmup phase of 2000 requests with the same prefix distribution to hit steady-state cache Hitrate. measure cold vs hot runs separately. target >=90% cache hit for steady state samples.
sasha: agreed. we should log cache hit rate per-request and aggregate by prefix length. also record per-request cache size and K/V eviction counts.
perf-bot: reminder: use --trace-kernel and --dump-batchmap flags so the CI artifacts include kernel timeline + batch composition.
marcus: metric defs proposal: TTFT = time from client request send to first token returned (client-side). TPOT = total time from send to last token / output tokens (avg per-token). p95/p99 computed over TTFT and TPOT separately. goodput = tokens accepted by app / wall-clock second (filters retries/errors). QPS = requests accepted / second.
anya: add: report p50/p95/p99 for both TTFT and per-token TPOT; also report tail-percentile of batch sizes and KV hitrates.
dex: for synthetic runs report achieved batching distribution (histogram), mean batch size, and effective GPU utilization. include a stress case with max batching to see throughput ceiling.
sasha: experiment matrix checklist (short):
- config snapshot (commit + model + quant profile)
- kernel logs + selection reasons
- batcher config + deterministic seed
- replay trace used (link to S3)
- warmup trace + steady-state window defined
- metrics: TTFT/TPOT p50/p95/p99, goodput, QPS, GPU util, KV hitrate
- artifacts: nvprof/metrics, batchmap csv, kernel timeline png
olga: regression detection: baseline every week, store canonical numbers per model+profile. fail CI on >10% p95 TTFT regression or >15% token-cost regression.
marcus: practical run commands (example):
```
./harness run --mode replay --trace s3://redwood-harness/traces/2026-02-15-prefixes.json --commit $SHA --quant int8 --trace-kernel --dump-batchmap --warmup 2000
```
sasha: reporting format: place a short summary in #eng-runtime with a one-line callout, then upload full artifacts to perf-bucket and link. include a small table: p95-TTFT, p99-TTFT, avg-TPOT, goodput tps, mean-batch-size.
anya: scoreboard item: make the harness output a small results.json with those canonical keys so dashboards can ingest automatically.
dex: also attach a small sample of raw requests (10) and the batch boundaries so we can re-run isolated failing cases.
sasha: OK owners: marucs will do kernel-timing plumbing, anya will add metrics keys + results.json, olga runs warmup Hitrate validation, dex tunes deterministic batcher. I'll coordinate the run and post summary.
marcus: SGTM, will push a branch with kernel timers today.
olga: I'll schedule warmup trace generation by EOD.
perf-bot: scheduled benchmark job: 1765432200 (expected finish ~1765432600). will post artifacts when done. :robot_face: 
sasha: thanks — aim to review next-day and flag regressions.
